identity.description:
Add the pool tooling and own-repo cases (D4b R2)

D4b revision R2: own-repo cases with pooled goldens. This PR adds the pool tooling. The six cases are built in the cases repo.

**Waits for D4b R1 and D4b R4.** The merge order is R1, R4, R2, R3. This PR does not move the pin in `eval/cases.json` and writes no baseline. When R1 and R4 merge, I rebase, merge the cases branch, move the pin, write the baseline at two repeats and re-derive the margins in this PR.

## What changes

- `pr-review pool <case-dir>... --out <dir> [--record <path>]... [--reviews <n>] [--write-golden]` builds the goldens of a case in six steps. (1) It runs two blind reviews by `claude-opus-5-5` and two by `gpt-6.1-sol` through the Codex CLI. No blind review sees a PR comment, a record or a golden. (2) It adds every reviewer finding of the PR's records. (3) It groups identical findings in code and the same defect by one `claude-sonnet-5-5` call. (4) It writes the anonymised `pool.json`, with `pool-key.json` apart. (5) It runs one Claude and one GPT adjudication per item and keeps an item only when both score 75 or more. (6) It joins kept items with overlapping spans and writes `golden.json` with the placeholder severity `unsure` for `pr-review label`. A case with no kept item is a clean case. `reviews.json` records what each blind review returned. A failed Codex call keeps the end of its stderr.
- `pr-review adjudicate <case-dir> (--record <path> --fingerprint <fp> | --finding <path>)` runs step 5 on one finding. D4b R3 uses it, or `adjudicateFinding` in `src/eval/pool/adjudicate.ts`, for a dismissed finding.
- The new case source is `pool`. The prompts are `prompts/pool-review.md`, `prompts/pool-group.md` and `prompts/pool-adjudicate.md`. The eval roles are pinned apart from the pipeline roles in `src/config/models.ts`.
- `src/eval/codex.ts` holds the Codex runner that the labeler and the pool share. The labeler tests do not change. `src/run.ts` gets a type-only change (`isEvalRole`).
- The README and design section 8 describe the pool. The design line that made records into goldens without labeling is removed, because the ticket says the eval takes no golden from a record.
- The version goes to 0.7.0.

## The cases (cases repo branch `r2-own-repo-cases`)

These are `pool-websites-130`, `pool-websites-114`, `pool-walle-14`, `pool-walle-16`, `pool-pr-review-15` and `pool-pr-review-17`: TypeScript and Python, from 34 to 271 added lines, with a feature, a refactor, two fixes and a config change. Each case uses the head that the first recorded run saw. A later head holds the fixes of the review findings, so it reviews clean.

The pool of four cases is finished: walle 14, walle 16 and websites 130 adjudicated to no item and are clean cases, and pr-review 15 kept one of two items. The pools of websites 114 and pr-review 17 stopped on the Codex account usage limit. They run again when the quota returns. Then `pr-review label` sets the severities, and the cases branch is pushed.

## Checks

`npm test` (1341 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

carried.claim: With --write-golden, golden.json is overwritten even when blind reviews or adjudication calls failed, so a quota failure can turn a case into a false clean case.
carried.evidence: if (opts.writeGolden) await writeFile(join(c.dir, "golden.json"), json({ findings: goldens }));
carried.suggested_fix: Skip the golden write (or refuse it) when any review failed or any item has the outcome failed.
carried.explanation: Failed calls make items not kept, and the code still writes the reduced golden list over the existing golden.json. The exit code 1 does not undo that write.

quotes: if (opts.writeGolden) await writeFile(join(c.dir, "golden.json"), json({ findings: goldens }));
verifier.rationale: With --write-golden, golden.json is written whatever happened earlier. A failed blind review adds no findings, and a failed adjudication gets the outcome "failed" and makes no golden. So when quota runs out, the golden list can be cut down or even empty, and that list still replaces the file. The CLI only sets exit code 1 after the write. The user sees the failure and can rerun or restore the file, so this fits a suggestion rather than a blocker.
